summary: In DeerFlow, a lead AI model does the work through tool calls and can hand tasks to sub-agents; a run normally ends when that model replies without asking for a tool, and plain code can also remove tool calls to bring it to a close. When a thread has an active /goal, a separate model call can judge whether the conversation shows the goal was met, though some conditions stand the goal down without that call.

judgments.question: Do the receipt ids a sub-agent cites in its report point to real, successful tool calls?
judgments.answer: When a task sub-agent completes and receipts were harvested, code checks its report's citations against them. Any verdict shown to the lead does not change the task status.

judgments.question: Did the run actually hand over the output files it produced?
judgments.answer: On normal completion, worker code uses available before and after snapshots to detect changed output files. If some are detected and none is covered by a recorded present_files path, the delivery check returns an error.

judgments.question: How many graph steps may one run take before it is stopped?
judgments.answer: The Gateway takes the request's recursion_limit if it is a positive integer, otherwise the configured default, and caps it at max_recursion_limit.

judgments.question: Is the agent stuck repeating the same tool calls, and should it be warned or stopped?
judgments.answer: After a model response with tool calls, code counts repeated call sets per run. With defaults, a repeated set can trigger a warning at 3 and a stop at 5; a separate window counting tool names has thresholds of 30 and 50. A stop removes that response's calls and adds a stop message.

judgments.question: How many turns may a sub-agent take?
judgments.answer: Code turns the sub-agent's max_turns (general-purpose 150, bash 60, config default 50) into a recursion limit.

judgments.question: Is there a free slot to run this sub-agent now, or must it queue or be refused?
judgments.answer: A process-wide admission controller (default 3 running) admits the execution, queues it up to max_queued with a timeout, or rejects it at once under the reject policy.

judgments.question: Did the provider stop because the output budget ran out, and if so must the possibly truncated tool calls be suppressed and the person told?
judgments.answer: Four detectors recognise the provider's output cap. On a hit all tool calls are removed, and a notice is added when tool calls were removed or no visible text remains.

judgments.question: How should the user's rough draft be rewritten before it is sent?
judgments.answer: On request, a one-shot model call rewrites the draft into a clearer instruction; the user decides whether to send it.

judgments.question: Is an inbound IM text a channel command or a chat turn?
judgments.answer: Code checks whether the first whitespace-delimited token is a known slash command, case-insensitively.

problems.title: web_fetch cuts page content at 4,096 characters, with no notice of the cut
problems.plain: Each web_fetch tool the map cites keeps at most the first 4,096 characters of the content it selects and adds no notice of that cut, so a long page can reach the model incomplete with nothing from the tool saying so. The example config uses the Jina tool, which does this. An open pull request proposes making the limit a setting.

verified.claimsPass: an independent AI reviewer from another company (OpenAI Codex, read-only) on 2026-11-08, in five rounds; each sentence it questioned was narrowed, removed or kept with the reason recorded

problems.title: One matching presented file is enough to pass the delivery check
problems.plain: On a normal completion, when changed output files are detected, the delivery check compares them with the paths recorded as presented. One presented path that covers a detected change satisfies the check, even if the run's other changed output files were not presented. The check is written to catch runs that present none of them.

problems.title: Fifty proposed calls to one tool can force a stop, even when each call differs
problems.plain: Besides counting repeated sets of tool calls, the loop check counts calls by tool name in a sliding window. At the default threshold, reaching 50 proposed calls to one tool in that window triggers a stop whatever their arguments: all calls in that response are removed and a stop message is added. A setting can raise the limit per tool. An open issue reports this limit interrupting batch scientific work, and a contributor there points to that setting.
